scenes.heading: Handling weather, no-shows, and reshoot policies

sents.d: Handling weather, no-shows, and reshoot policies
Decide your policy before the first bad-weather day, not during a stressful phone call.

Outdoor shoots eventually collide with rain, a client running very late, or a no-show — having a written policy for each (in your contract, not improvised in the moment) protects both your schedule and the relationship.

scenes.heading: One free reschedule, then a fee

sents.d: A common approach: one free reschedule for weather or client-caused delays within a set notice window, with a smaller fee for a second reschedule or a true no-show, since your time was already blocked off.
Stating this clearly during booking — not as a threat, just as normal business practice — actually reassures most clients rather than putting them off, since it shows you run things professionally.

take: Write weather and no-show policies into your contract.
